name: sandbox-policy
description: The sandbox@1 provider `declarative`: the DECISION layer of the confinement seam. Policy comes from this plugin's config (per-resource rules, fail-closed by default), the decision is pure (definitions/sandbox.ts) and no host resource is ever touched: consumers (fs@1, subprocess@1, jobs@1, computer-use, browser-use) ask for a decision and apply it themselves.

config.description: The policy itself: what an unconfigured resource gets, the defaults every resource starts from, and one rule per resource name.

source.description: Label of this policy, reported by the `sandbox policy` tool (default sandbox@1).

unconfigured.description: What a resource with NO rule and NO defaults gets: `deny` (fail-closed, the default) answers with reason sandbox.no-policy, `allow` grants the built-in defaults.

approvalRequired.description: Every call of this policy needs an explicit approval (a call without approvalGranted is denied).

defaults.description: The rule every resource starts from: mode (read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access), readRoots, writeRoots, env (NAME allow-list), network (none | allow-list | unrestricted, plus hosts), limits (cpuSeconds, memoryBytes, nofile, wallTimeMs, maxOutputBytes, maxProcesses), approvalRequired, dropPrivileges, allowCommands, denyCommands, deny.

resources.description: One rule per resource NAME (fs, subprocess, jobs, computer-use, browser-use, or any custom name); a rule narrows the defaults and can DENY the resource outright with `deny: true` (deny precedence).
